sheet-91-1.description: The lower right block of sheet 91 covers the two blocks between Avenue B at the top and Avenue A at the bottom, from South Avenue on the left to Bay Avenue on the right, in the residential grid west of the Atlantic Highlands business district. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, as on sheet 92, which adjoins it across Avenue B. Most lots are numbered within the Hubbard Tract, whose name is lettered across the left block, and the frame dwellings are mostly one to two and a half storeys. Named buildings include the Strassburger Cottage, the Johnson Cottage and The Normandie on the right block, and toward Avenue A a livery stable, a blacksmith shop and the O. B. Irwin carriage manufactory with its painting shop. A plumbing shop and a livery stand on the left block, and one dwelling is marked as badly damaged by fire. Water pipes of 4 inches run along Avenue B and Center Avenue, and fire hydrants are marked at the corners. The south side of Avenue A lies on sheet 93 and is not drawn here, and Bay Avenue is cut at the right edge of the sheet.
notes: Avenue A and Avenue B keep their names today; Avenue A's south side is off the sheet, so its junctions were hand-picked from the north edge plus half the street width.

map, 60 ft. Six blocks separated by heavy lines: top left Central R.R. of New Jersey pier and steamboat wharf on Sandy Hook Bay (north drawn up); top right title, town description and key map (not to scale, not configured); middle left municipal water works and Lincoln Av at the railroad; middle right Asbury Av, Valley Drive and 1st Av (north up-left); bottom left Washington, Highland and Mount Avs north of 1st Av; bottom right Avenues A and B between South and Bay Avs. Configured: part 1 bottom right, part 4 middle right, part 5 bottom left.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Central R.R. of New Jersey pier and steamboat wharf, Sandy Hook Bay (no street junction; the pier no longer exists; needs a carried point from part 3 where the tracks cross the dividing line, once part 3 is placed, plus north_deg; low value).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Atlantic Highlands municipal water works, Lincoln Avenue north of the railroad (no street junction (Lincoln Av ends at the railroad, which is now the Henry Hudson Trail); needs step 6b: locate.py extend West Lincoln Avenue to the Henry Hudson Trail, plus px_per_ft 6.62 and north_deg about 72).

sheet-91-4.description: The middle right block of sheet 91 shows the junction of Asbury Avenue, Valley Drive and 1st Avenue at the south edge of the Atlantic Highlands business district, with the Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks crossing the left side of the block on a curve. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned differently from the rest of the sheet, with its north arrow pointing up and to the left. North of Asbury Avenue stands the Mickens and McHenry planing mill and lumber shed with a hardware and paint store, a smoking room and small sheds, and a small lumber pile lies beside the railroad. South of Asbury Avenue is the W. W. Leonard contractor's yard with an open coal bin, a carpenter shop and an office. On the east side of 1st Avenue there are a few dwellings and a stable, and Valley Drive runs off to the right with a 6 inch water pipe along it. Most of the block is open ground. Lot numbers 15 to 29 line Asbury Avenue.
notes: Asbury Avenue no longer reaches 1st Avenue; Memorial Parkway (NJ 36) now meets 1st Avenue on the line of the old junction, which was used as the single control point.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey line is abandoned; its right-of-way is the Henry Hudson Trail.

sheet-91-5.description: The lower left block of sheet 91 covers the area north of 1st Avenue between Washington Avenue and Mount Avenue, beside the Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks that cross the top of the block toward the pier. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The name The Atlantic Highlands Association is lettered across the lots. Along Mount Avenue and Highland Avenue are the John J. Leonard coal and wood yard with a wood sawing shed and a coal dump by the tracks, the Lyceum Theatre with its stage and scenery building, the Monmouth office press, a bake house with storage and tenements, a millinery shop and a bakery. Between Highland and Washington Avenues stand a Negro church, a Knights of Pythias hall and a printing office among scattered dwellings, and a railroad freight watchman's box stands by the tracks. Water pipes of 8 and 10 inches run along 1st Avenue and the avenues. Railroad Avenue is lettered at the right edge beyond Mount Avenue. A scale of 60 feet to an inch is printed at the bottom left.
notes: Today West Washington Avenue, West Highland Avenue and West Mount Avenue (the East and West names divide at 1st Avenue).
Railroad Avenue is printed as R.R. Ave.

sheet-92.description: Sheet 92 covers the residential district west of the Atlantic Highlands business area, from Highland Avenue on the left to Bay Avenue on the right and from Avenue B at the bottom to beyond Avenue D, which crosses the upper part of the sheet on a slant. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The blocks are laid out in narrow numbered lots of the Hubbard Tract, lettered across the lower blocks, with mostly two and two and a half storey frame dwellings. St. Agnes Roman Catholic Church and its priest's house stand on South Avenue, and the 1st Baptist Church stands in the Joseph Bowne Estate north of Avenue D. Named houses include The West End, The Cresson, the Ideal Villa, the Morris Cottage, the Martin Cottage and the Many Mind Cottage. A windmill and water tank stand in the upper right block. Most of the large block between Highland and South Avenues north of Avenue C is open land. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches run along the avenues, with fire hydrants at most corners.
notes: Highland Avenue here is today West Highland Avenue.
map, 60 ft. Avenues B, C and D between Highland and Bay Avs; St. Agnes R.C. Church, 1st Baptist Church. Drawn with north to the upper right (about 72 degrees).

sheet-93.description: Sheet 93 covers the business district of Atlantic Highlands and the shore of Sandy Hook Bay, from Avenue A on the left to 3rd Avenue on the right and from Mount Avenue at the bottom to the bay. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that 1st Avenue runs up the sheet, unlike the neighbouring sheets. Stores, offices, a bank, a post office, the Columbus Hotel, a garage, liveries and a drug store line both sides of 1st Avenue, with the Homestead Block on Railroad Avenue. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs up the middle of the sheet past its passenger station and pump house, with a track on trestle curving out toward the pier, which is shown on sheet 91. Many Mind Creek winds through the left half to the bay, crossed by wooden bridges at Bay Avenue and Center Avenue. Near the shore are the Grand View Hotel, the Hopping and Ely lumber yard, an open platform for dancing, fish markets and a bulkhead along Bay View Avenue. The Commercial Hotel stands on Avenue A and the Bay View House on Bay View Avenue. A beach cottage and bath houses occupy the upper left corner.
notes: Bay View Avenue is today Ocean Boulevard.
Mount Avenue at the bottom is today East Mount Avenue east of 1st Avenue and West Mount Avenue west of it.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey line and pier are gone; the right-of-way is the Henry Hudson Trail.
The association name is printed Assoc'n.

map, 60 ft. Business district: 1st Av from Mount Av to the shore, Bay Av, Center Av, Railroad Av, Bay View Av (now Ocean Boulevard), C.R.R. of N.J. station and tracks to the pier, Many Mind Creek. Turned on the page: 1st Av runs up the sheet (north about -14 degrees), unlike the other sheets.

sheet-94.description: Sheet 94 covers the residential district south of the Atlantic Highlands business area, from Garfield Avenue on the left to Mount Avenue on the right and from 1st Avenue at the top to beyond 7th Avenue at the bottom. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The name The Atlantic Highlands Association is lettered across the blocks, which are divided into narrow numbered lots with mostly two and two and a half storey frame dwellings and many vacant lots on the western blocks. The High School stands on Lincoln Avenue, the Presbyterian Church on Washington Avenue and the Central Baptist Church on Highland Avenue at 3rd Avenue. Near 1st Avenue at the upper right are stores, a tin shop, a livery and a grocery, and the Hopping and Ely lumber yard reaches the top edge. Named houses include the Evelyn, the Eureka, the Glen Cottage, the Sunset, the Breeze, the Oakland Cottage and Fruit Vale. Lettering at the right edge names 2d, 4th and 6th Avenues and Eighth Avenue, which continue on sheet 95.
notes: Garfield, Lincoln, Washington, Highland and Mount Avenues are today East Garfield, East Lincoln, East Washington, East Highland and East Mount Avenue.
map, 60 ft. 1st, 3rd and 7th Avs between Garfield and Mount Avs; High School, Presbyterian and Central Baptist churches. North to the upper right (about 72 degrees).

sheet-95-1.description: The main part of sheet 95 covers the eastern residential district of Atlantic Highlands between Mount Avenue on the left and Bay View Avenue and the Sandy Hook Bay shore on the right, from 3rd Avenue at the top to 8th Avenue and Grand Avenue at the bottom. It is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Its most distinctive feature is the concentric plan of The Atlantic Highlands Association: 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th Avenues and Prospect Avenue curve in rings around a circular central lot, with radiating lot lines. The blocks hold mostly two and two and a half storey frame dwellings, among them the Lockwood House, the Emery Cottage, the Brandon, Buena Vista, Sea Gulls and the Sea View with the Sea View Cottage. The M. E. Church and its parsonage stand on 3rd Avenue. A public park lies along Bay View Avenue, and Bath Avenue leads to bathing houses, a private pier and a Bay View pavilion on the shore. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs along the top of the bluff by the bay. The inset at the lower right is a separate part.
notes: Bay View Avenue is today Ocean Boulevard; its junctions carry residuals of about 3 m.
Mount Avenue is today East Mount Avenue; Prospect Avenue is today Prospect Circle.
map, 60 ft. Mount Av to Bay View Av (now Ocean Boulevard), 3rd to 8th Avs and the circular Prospect Av; M.E. Church. Inset at bottom right (part 2): The Casino on Bay View Av, not configured.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Casino and public park on Bay View Avenue (Ocean Boulevard) (no street junction; only one street drawn; needs a parcel corner or a feature shared with sheet 95 part 1).
